source_documents.title: PH-FS-014 v1.6 — Guided Buying & Approval Framework
PH-FS-021 v1.2 — Supplier Enablement & Invoice Automation

impacts.current_roles: All employees with a buying need — engineering, marketing, R&D, admin. Majority raise fewer than 10 requests a year.
impacts.as_is: Requisitioner emails a free-form request to the shared procurement mailbox and waits. No standard form and no status visibility; chasing by email is the norm. Around a third of requests are returned for a missing cost centre or specification.
impacts.to_be: Requisitioner self-serves in Guided Buying: picks a category tile, buys from a catalogue or completes a structured non-catalogue form, and tracks status themselves. Cost centre, GL, delivery site and required-by date are mandatory at entry — the request cannot be submitted incomplete.
impacts.people_impact: New activity performed with existing resources: the requisitioner now does the data entry and status tracking that Procurement did for them. No new skills beyond the tool itself, but a real shift in who is responsible for getting the request right first time.
impacts.process_impact: Significant change to the process steps and to where the process starts. Ownership of request quality hands off from Procurement to the requisitioner, and the mandatory-field gate is a new step with no predecessor.
impacts.tech_impact: New system for this population — Guided Buying replaces email entirely. The largest single group of new users in the programme.
impacts.other_impacts:
Policy: none directly, but the mandatory-field gate enforces data standards that were previously advisory.
Data: requisitioner now owns cost centre and GL accuracy at source.
impacts.benefit_narrative: You can see exactly where your order is without chasing anyone, and most orders approve within a day instead of taking 12–18.
impacts.training_timing: T-2 weeks, reinforced at point of use
impacts.key_message: You'll raise requests yourself in a guided shopping-style tool instead of emailing Procurement — and for the first time you'll be able to see where your order is.
impacts.comms_channel: Town hall; line-manager cascade; intranet; in-app announcement; demo video
impacts.comms_owner: Chief Operating Officer (awareness); line managers (personal impact)
impacts.mitigation_actions: Do not rely on scheduled training for this group — they will have forgotten it by their next transaction. Point-of-use in-app guidance plus a one-page job aid is the primary channel; the course is secondary.
impacts.notes: Headcount excludes the DE entity (Wave 2). Confirm the final Wave 1 population against go-live scope — INT-02 flagged this as unresolved.

impacts.current_roles: Facilities coordinators; IT asset and service coordinators
impacts.as_is: High-frequency requisitioners email several requests a week and maintain informal relationships with named buyers to expedite. Urgent items are handled by 'a phone call and a favour'.
impacts.to_be: Same Guided Buying flow as all requisitioners, but used daily. This group hits catalogue rules, non-catalogue thresholds and the triage queue routinely, and becomes the de-facto super-user population in their functions.
impacts.people_impact: New activity with existing resources, at high frequency. Also loses the informal expediting route through named buyers, which is how urgent work gets done today — a behavioural change, not just a task change.
impacts.process_impact: Significant change to the process steps and to the escalation path. The informal fast lane closes and is replaced by rules the user has to plan around.
impacts.tech_impact: New system, used daily rather than occasionally.
impacts.other_impacts: Engagement: this group is the natural super-user and champion population for their functions.
impacts.benefit_narrative: No more chasing procurement for status — you raise, track and receipt your own orders, and repeat buys take minutes.
impacts.training_timing: T-3 weeks, plus super-user session at T-5 weeks
impacts.key_message: You'll do more of your own buying end to end — and the informal 'call a buyer' route is replaced by rules you can see and plan around.
impacts.comms_channel: Targeted email; super-user briefing; drop-in sessions
impacts.comms_owner: Head of Facilities; Head of IT Operations
impacts.mitigation_actions: Recruit 8–10 of this group as change champions ahead of go-live — they are the highest-volume users and will set the tone for their functions.

impacts.current_roles: Engineers, R&D scientists and technical leads specifying bespoke goods and services
impacts.as_is: Everything is bought free-text. Requisitioners describe what they want in their own words and Procurement sources it. No restriction on what can be requested or from whom.
impacts.to_be: Buying channel is fixed by category: catalogue mandatory for IT Hardware, Stationery and MRO; a structured non-catalogue form is permitted for Engineering Services, R&D Consumables and Facilities Works; anything above €100k must go through a sourcing event. There is no free-text 'other' option.
impacts.people_impact: High behavioural and mindset shift. This group loses the discretion to describe and source what it wants in its own terms, and has already said in a workshop that it will work around the constraint: 'if the system won't let me describe what I actually need, I'll go around it'.
impacts.process_impact: Added and deleted process steps — a structured form with mandatory specification replaces a free-text email, and unmatched requests route to a new 2-day triage queue.
impacts.tech_impact: New system, with the category rules enforced in the interface rather than by a person.
impacts.other_impacts: Policy: this is a control change presented as a system change — free-text purchasing is withdrawn (FS-01 §2.3). Engagement: highest workaround risk in the register; track non-catalogue form use vs. triage-queue volume in the first 8 weeks as the early warning signal.
impacts.benefit_narrative: Catalogue items arrive faster and at pre-negotiated prices; the non-catalogue form still exists for genuinely bespoke work in your categories.
impacts.key_message: Bespoke technical buying still has a route — the non-catalogue form is open for Engineering Services and R&D Consumables. What changes is that it's a structured form, not an email.
impacts.comms_channel: Function-specific briefing; drop-in Q&A with category leads; FAQ
impacts.mitigation_actions: Run a category-channel review workshop with Engineering and R&D before design freeze. The stated intent to 'go around it' is a live workaround risk — the fastest way to close it is to let this group test the non-catalogue form against real recent requisitions and adjust the category rules where it genuinely does not fit.

impacts.current_roles: Cost centre owners; department heads; category approvers; Finance Director
impacts.as_is: The buyer looks up the approver on a SharePoint DOA spreadsheet last properly updated around 18 months ago, then emails them. The approver replies 'approved' by email, usually without line-item detail, and the buyer files the email as evidence. Approvers routinely approve items above their actual authority.
impacts.to_be: Approval routes automatically from a DOA mastered off the HR org structure. The approver receives a task with full line-item detail and can approve, reject or return for edit only — no approval above their limit, no editing of line values, no self-approval. Unactioned tasks escalate to their line manager after 3 working days.
impacts.people_impact: New activity using existing resources — approving in a system rather than by email reply, with the detail now in front of them. Modest task change, but a real shift for approvers used to signing off on trust.
impacts.process_impact: Simplified through automation: routing, evidence capture and escalation all become system steps, and the manual DOA lookup disappears.
impacts.tech_impact: New system for this population, including a mobile app for approvals.
impacts.other_impacts: Policy: the DOA becomes enforced rather than advisory — no override path (FS-01 §3.3). The workshop read this as a small change because most assumed enforced limits already existed; nobody could state their own limit correctly. Expect a spike in rejected approvals in week one.
impacts.benefit_narrative: You'll see what you're actually approving, on your phone, and you'll stop being asked to sign off things that were never yours to sign.
impacts.key_message: Approvals move to your Ariba inbox with full detail — and the system will hold you to your actual limit, which may be lower than what you've been approving.
impacts.comms_channel: Targeted email with personalised DOA limit; line-manager cascade; FAQ
impacts.mitigation_actions: Send every approver their personal DOA limit in writing at T-4 weeks. Do not let go-live be the moment someone discovers their limit changed.

impacts.current_roles: Cost centre owners and budget holders who currently manage spend around approval thresholds
impacts.as_is: No aggregation. Purchases can be split across multiple requests to stay under an approval limit; this happens openly and is not treated as a control breach.
impacts.to_be: The system aggregates requests from the same requester, cost centre and supplier over a rolling 30 days and routes to the next approval tier once the aggregate crosses a threshold. The split-purchase route closes.
impacts.people_impact: Minimal change in activity — nothing new to do. The change is behavioural: an established practice that people describe openly, without recognising it as a control issue, stops working.
impacts.process_impact: Minor change to the process steps. Routing logic changes behind the scenes; the approver's own steps are unchanged.
impacts.tech_impact: No additional system change beyond the approval move already covered by CI-004.
impacts.other_impacts: Policy: closes the split-purchase gap (FS-01 §3.4). This is the clearest case in the register of low impact magnitude with high resistance — the control is trivial to build and the behaviour it closes is considered normal.
impacts.benefit_narrative: Fewer surprises at year end — committed spend is visible against your budget in real time rather than arriving as a monthly report.
impacts.key_message: Repeat purchases to the same supplier now add up against your limit over 30 days — plan the whole spend up front rather than in instalments.
impacts.comms_channel: Targeted email; finance business partner 1:1s
impacts.mitigation_actions: Frame this as a policy that already existed rather than a new restriction, and have Finance Business Partners raise it in existing 1:1s rather than in a broadcast. A public announcement invites the affected group to defend current practice; a private conversation does not.

impacts.current_roles: All requisitioners and named delivery contacts
impacts.as_is: The AP team performs goods receipt centrally from delivery paperwork. Requisitioners do nothing after their order is placed.
impacts.to_be: The named delivery contact on the requisition — by default the requisitioner — confirms receipt in Guided Buying or the mobile app. No invoice is paid without a receipt.
impacts.people_impact: Net-new accountability moving from a central team to several thousand individuals. Each instance is small but it is an addition to the day job that nobody asked for and most do not yet know is coming.
impacts.process_impact: Significant change to hand-offs of process ownership: goods receipt moves out of AP and into the business, and becomes a payment-blocking step.
impacts.tech_impact: New system and a new mobile interaction for a population that otherwise touches the system only when buying.
impacts.other_impacts: Control: non-receipt directly blocks supplier payment, so low compliance becomes an AP and supplier-relations problem within weeks. Instrument overdue receipts by cost centre from day one — the ageing report is the only reliable early signal.
impacts.benefit_narrative: Confirming receipt takes seconds on your phone and it's what gets your supplier paid on time — which is what stops them chasing you.
impacts.key_message: When your order arrives, confirm it in the app. It takes seconds, and it's the step that gets your supplier paid.
impacts.comms_channel: In-app prompt; job aid; line-manager cascade; automated overdue-receipt reminder
impacts.mitigation_actions: Track overdue receipts by cost centre weekly and route the list to line managers, not to individuals. This is the impact most likely to quietly fail.

impacts.l4: Automated PO Generation — Buyer Role Redesign
impacts.current_roles: 14 Buyers; 3 Buying Team Leads (UK 6, DE 4, PL 4 + leads)
impacts.as_is: Buyers receive ~900 email requisitions a month, chase missing data on about a third, manually key them into ECC, look up approvers on the SharePoint DOA, chase approvals, create the PO and email it to the supplier as a PDF. Pricing knowledge is held personally — 'my price list is in my head and in a spreadsheet on my desktop'.
impacts.to_be: Catalogue and approved non-catalogue orders create and transmit automatically with no buyer involvement. Buyer intervention is retained only for non-catalogue requests above €50k and exception-flagged requests. The role shifts from transaction processing to category support, exception handling and supplier performance.
impacts.people_impact: The largest role change in the programme. Major decrease in current work effort, new skills required, and a high mindset shift — the team asked twice, unprompted, 'so the system decides the price now? What am I for?'. Personal pricing knowledge becomes catalogue and contract data, which is a loss of individual standing as well as of task.
impacts.process_impact: Significant change to process steps and to ownership and accountability: the majority of the team's daily process is automated away, and what remains is exception work with a different rhythm.
impacts.tech_impact: New system replacing the ECC transactions this team lives in daily.
impacts.other_impacts:
Engagement: the last ERP go-live is the reference point everyone reaches for. The Head of Procurement Operations, unprompted: "the last ERP go-live, we had two days of training six weeks before and then nothing. Half the team never used it properly. Whatever happens this time, that can't be the plan" (INT-03 @00:04:39). The EMEA Team Lead says the same in INT-01 and is the credibility test for this workstream — engage directly, not through the cascade.
Delivery constraint: the PL team (4 buyers) flagged that all previous-programme training was English-only and UK-time.
impacts.benefit_narrative: You stop keying other people's requisitions and start doing the category and supplier work you were hired for — but this only lands if the new role is described concretely and soon.
impacts.training_timing: T-5 weeks, plus floorwalking T-0 to T+4
impacts.key_message: Transactional buying is being automated. Your role moves to category support, exceptions and supplier performance — here is what that looks like, in writing, before go-live.
impacts.comms_channel: Team session with the Procurement Director; 1:1s with each buyer; written role description
impacts.comms_owner: Procurement Director (with each buyer's own line manager for the 1:1s)
impacts.mitigation_actions: Issue written to-be role descriptions before the first training session. Asking this team to learn a system that removes their current job, without telling them what the new job is, will read as an answer to the 'what am I for' question that nobody intends. Confirm PL localisation and scheduling before the training calendar is published.

impacts.current_roles: Supplier sales, order management and account teams
impacts.as_is: The supplier receives a PDF purchase order by email from a named buyer and confirms informally by reply. Order queries go to the buyer directly.
impacts.to_be: The supplier receives the PO through the Ariba Network and confirms the order in the Network. Order status, changes and confirmations are transacted in the Network rather than by email with a named individual.
impacts.people_impact: New activity using existing resources for an external audience. The material change is losing the named-buyer relationship as the route for order queries.
impacts.process_impact: Added and deleted process steps: order confirmation becomes a system transaction rather than an email reply, and the query route changes.
impacts.tech_impact: New system for the supplier, adopted on the client's timetable and outside the supplier's control.
impacts.other_impacts: Commercial: this group carries ~90% of spend and supplier non-adoption is a leading cause of Ariba benefit shortfall. Track enablement completion weekly against the T-10 target and escalate laggards to their Category Manager — once it slips this is a schedule risk, not a comms risk.
impacts.benefit_narrative: Orders arrive in a single channel with confirmed detail, and you can see PO and payment status yourself instead of emailing for it.
impacts.training_timing: T-10 to T-8 weeks, repeated across time zones
impacts.key_message: From January, Meridian orders come to you through the Ariba Network. Register now — suppliers who aren't enabled can't receive orders.
impacts.comms_channel: Supplier letter from the Procurement Director; enablement webinars; supplier portal; account-manager calls for the top 50
impacts.mitigation_actions: Named-contact enablement calls for the top 50 suppliers by spend rather than broadcast-only.

impacts.current_roles: Small supplier owners, office managers and finance contacts
impacts.as_is: The supplier is set up by the client's Master Data team from information supplied by email. The supplier does nothing beyond sending their details once.
impacts.to_be: The supplier self-registers on the Ariba Network and completes a qualification questionnaire covering financial, compliance, ESG and information security criteria, then maintains their own contact, bank, tax and certification data on an ongoing basis. Suppliers not registered cannot be transacted with.
impacts.people_impact: New ongoing activity for a group with no obligation to invest effort — registration and data upkeep move onto the supplier, using their own resources.
impacts.process_impact: Added process steps: registration, qualification and ongoing data maintenance are all new to this audience.
impacts.tech_impact: New system, self-service, with no client-side hand-holding for tranche 3.
impacts.other_impacts: Policy: registration is mandatory to keep trading (FS-02 §1.1). Commercial: this group is ~10% of spend, so the client has little leverage and the supplier little incentive. The realistic failure mode is not resistance but silence, discovered at go-live when a PO cannot be raised. Tranche 3 (~400 suppliers) has no assigned enablement owner (FS-02 §4).
impacts.benefit_narrative: One free account, one place to see orders and payment status, and no more chasing us for remittance information.
impacts.key_message: Register on the Ariba Network before January or we won't be able to raise orders to you. It's free and takes about 20 minutes.
impacts.comms_channel: Supplier letter; step-by-step registration guide; supplier helpdesk; reminders at T-8, T-6, T-4, T-2
impacts.mitigation_actions: Assign an owner for tranche 3 self-service enablement — FS-02 §4 records this as unassigned and it will not resolve itself. Agree the fallback for non-enabled tail suppliers after T+8 weeks before go-live: the decision (block, extend, or offboard) has commercial consequences needing Procurement Director sign-off.
impacts.notes: Tranche 3 population (~400) is an estimate from the spend analysis, not a validated list. Confirm against the vendor master before the enablement campaign is sized.

impacts.current_roles: Master data analysts; Compliance reviewer; Finance approver
impacts.as_is: Supplier records are created and amended centrally from emailed information. Ownership of supplier master data is genuinely unclear — Finance believes Procurement owns it and Procurement believes Finance does.
impacts.to_be: Suppliers maintain their own contact, bank, tax, insurance and certification data. The Master Data team moves from creating records to reviewing and approving supplier-submitted changes. Bank detail changes require dual approval by Compliance and Finance plus a call-back verification.
impacts.people_impact: The team's core activity is removed and replaced by a control and review function, with a new fraud-prevention obligation attached. New skills required; small team, high per-person impact.
impacts.process_impact: Significant change to process steps and to ownership: record creation moves outside the organisation and the team's remaining process is a control gate that does not exist today.
impacts.tech_impact: New system replacing ECC vendor master maintenance.
impacts.other_impacts:
Policy: new dual-approval and call-back control on bank detail changes (FS-02 §1.2).
OPEN DECISION: the pre-existing ownership ambiguity between Finance and Procurement means there is currently no single accountable owner to design the new operating model with — this needs a Steering Committee decision, not stakeholder engagement.
impacts.benefit_narrative: You stop rekeying supplier details from emails and take on the control role — reviewing and approving changes rather than typing them.
impacts.key_message: Suppliers will maintain their own data. Your role becomes reviewing and approving what they submit — including a new dual-approval control on bank details.
impacts.comms_channel: Team session; 1:1 with each analyst; written role description
impacts.mitigation_actions: Resolve supplier master data ownership between Finance and Procurement before designing the review workflow. Escalate to the Steering Committee — the control cannot be operated without an accountable owner.
impacts.notes: OPEN QUESTION: who owns supplier master data today, and who will own the review-and-approve function at go-live? INT-01 records Finance and Procurement each believing it is the other.

impacts.current_roles: AP clerks (7 UK, 4 PL); AP Team Lead
impacts.as_is: AP keys every invoice from PDF or paper, matches manually against the PO, and performs goods receipt centrally from delivery paperwork. The team also handles ~400 supplier payment queries a month through a shared mailbox.
impacts.to_be: Suppliers submit invoices through the Ariba Network; three-way match runs automatically within tolerance. AP handles exceptions only — price and quantity mismatch, missing goods receipt, blocked supplier, duplicate, tax code failure. Suppliers self-serve payment status and the shared mailbox is targeted for decommissioning at T+6 months.
impacts.people_impact: Major decrease in work effort with new skills required. The design targets 85% touchless against a current baseline of 0%, and the business case assumes ~70% less transactional effort. The team's entire current workload is the thing being automated.
impacts.process_impact: Significant change to process steps and to ownership: data entry and matching disappear, goods receipt moves out to the business, and what remains is exception triage.
impacts.tech_impact: New system replacing the ECC transactions the team works in all day.
impacts.other_impacts:
PEOPLE RISK — highest in the register: FS-02 §2.3 records that the business case assumes redeployment rather than reduction, but that this has never been confirmed to the team in writing. From where they sit, the honest reading is that the programme removes 70% of their work with no stated consequence.
Dependency: the 85% touchless target is conditional on CI-006 goods-receipt compliance across 3,620 occasional users. If receipting lags, AP exception volume rises rather than falls and the redeployment case weakens.
impacts.benefit_narrative: Only meaningful once the redeployment position is stated. Until then this group has been given a number and no answer.
impacts.training_timing: T-4 weeks, plus hypercare T-0 to T+4
impacts.key_message: Invoice matching is being automated and your role becomes exception management. Here is what the team looks like after go-live — including headcount.
impacts.comms_channel: Team session with the CFO; 1:1s; written statement of the redeployment position
impacts.comms_owner: Chief Financial Officer (position statement); AP Team Lead (day-to-day)
impacts.mitigation_actions: Get the redeployment position confirmed in writing and communicated before AP training begins. An 11-person team is being asked to build the system that removes most of their current work, while the answer to 'what happens to us' exists only as an untested assumption in a business case. Escalate to the CFO with a date.
impacts.notes: Flag the CI-006 dependency to the Steering Committee explicitly — the benefit case for this impact rests on a behaviour change in a different stakeholder group.

impacts.current_roles: Supplier accounts receivable and billing teams
impacts.as_is: The supplier emails a PDF invoice or posts paper to the AP shared mailbox, then chases payment status by email or phone.
impacts.to_be: The supplier submits invoices through the Ariba Network by PO-flip, cXML integration or Network-hosted entry. Paper and PDF-email invoicing is decommissioned for enabled suppliers at go-live. Payment status is self-served in the Network.
impacts.people_impact: New activity using existing resources in the supplier's own billing team. No new skills of substance, but the existing channel is withdrawn rather than deprecated.
impacts.process_impact: Significant change: a hard cutover at T+0 (FS-02 §2.1), so a supplier who has not adopted the new channel simply stops being able to bill. Tolerance rules also mean invoices previously resolved by a phone call to AP now reject automatically.
impacts.tech_impact: New system for invoice submission, replacing email and post entirely.
impacts.other_impacts: Policy: ±2% or €50 price tolerance, 0% on quantity. Publish the tolerances to suppliers before go-live so rejections are predictable rather than mysterious, and staff the supplier helpdesk above steady-state for the first 6 weeks.
impacts.benefit_narrative: Invoices matched automatically get paid without chasing, and you can see payment status yourself instead of emailing AP.
impacts.training_timing: T-6 weeks, repeated across time zones
impacts.key_message: From go-live we can only accept invoices through the Ariba Network — PDF and paper invoices will not be processed. Matched invoices get paid without chasing.
impacts.comms_channel: Supplier letter; enablement webinar; step-by-step invoicing guide; supplier helpdesk
impacts.mitigation_actions: Publish match tolerances to suppliers before go-live and over-staff the helpdesk for the first 6 weeks.

impacts.current_roles: 8 Category Managers across 4 categories
impacts.as_is: The Category Manager emails suppliers individually, builds a comparison spreadsheet by hand and negotiates second rounds by phone. Bids are visible only to the Category Manager until they make a recommendation — a standing audit finding. Nothing but the final number is recorded.
impacts.to_be: Events are built from templates and published to all invited suppliers simultaneously. Bids are sealed and invisible to everyone, including the Category Manager, until the event closes. Comparison is auto-generated, scoring is entered against pre-declared weighted criteria, and the award rationale is recorded in-system as the audit trail. Second-round negotiation runs as a further in-system round; offline negotiation is not supported. All spend above €100k must go through a competitive event.
impacts.people_impact: High mindset shift and new skills. Sealed bidding removes this group's privileged early sight of bid data, in-system scoring makes their judgement visible and challengeable, and removing offline negotiation takes away what they consider their core skill. A Category Manager, on second-round negotiation: "That's a phone call. Always has been. That's — I mean, that's the job, isn't it. That's where I actually earn my money. You don't get another four percent out of somebody through a portal" (INT-03 @00:01:08). The same speaker was explicit that he is not opposed in principle — "get the admin off me and I'll be the first one cheering" (@00:04:25) — so this is a defence of professional identity, not of the status quo.
impacts.process_impact: Significant change to process steps and to accountability — every element changes at once: the channel, the transparency model, the negotiation method and the mandate.
impacts.tech_impact: New system replacing email, Excel and the telephone as the sourcing toolset.
impacts.other_impacts:
Policy: the €100k competitive sourcing mandate converts a policy expectation into an enforced control (SIG-02). The group's own read is that this is not new policy but newly enforceable — "That's already the policy. Has been for years. The difference is nobody could check before and now the system won't let you past it" (INT-03 @00:03:10).

Audit: closes the standing finding on bid visibility, which INT-03 @00:00:31 confirms was raised in two consecutive years without action.

OPEN DESIGN GAP: there is no known waiver route for genuinely urgent sourcing. Today it is a phone call to the Head of Procurement Ops. Asked directly whether a waiver exists in the new model, nobody in the room knew (INT-03 @00:03:49). Same pattern as CI-018.
impacts.benefit_narrative: Two days a week back. In their own words: "Not building the comparison by hand. That's two days of my week gone, every week, copying numbers into a spreadsheet. If the system does that I'd take it tomorrow" (INT-03 @00:04:05).
impacts.training_timing: T-6 weeks, plus a live pilot event at T-4
impacts.key_message: Sourcing moves in-system with sealed bids and recorded rationale. Negotiation doesn't disappear — it becomes a structured round with an audit trail behind it.
impacts.comms_channel: Team workshop with the Procurement Director; 1:1s; pilot event debrief
impacts.mitigation_actions: Run a real sourcing event in the system with this group before go-live rather than a training exercise — this is a small, expert, sceptical population and hands-on proof will move them further than any briefing. Involve them in designing the scoring criteria templates: they asked to be, unprompted and as the closing remark of the discovery session — "we've not been asked about the scoring criteria and I'd like to be" (INT-03 @00:04:59). That is an unusually cheap opportunity to convert the most sceptical group into co-designers.
impacts.notes: Volume disputed on the record: one Category Manager put team-wide sourcing events at "a hundred and forty, hundred and fifty" a year, and a colleague immediately corrected it to "closer to two hundred" once informal three-quote exercises are counted (INT-03 @00:02:24). Neither figure is banked — see CI-021, which exists because of that exchange. Confirm event volume from the spend analysis before it drives any training or licence sizing.

impacts.l4: Low-Value Three-Quote Sourcing — Brought Into the System
impacts.current_roles: Category Managers running informal three-quote exercises alongside their logged events
impacts.as_is: Low-value sourcing is done by ringing round three suppliers and raising a PO against the best price. It is not logged as a sourcing event, no record is kept beyond the PO, and it does not appear in any reported event volume. On the team's own account this is a substantial share of all sourcing activity.
impacts.to_be: All sourcing runs through the system. Informal three-quote exercises either become recorded events or stop, and the activity becomes visible for the first time.
impacts.people_impact: New activity using existing resources: work that was a phone call and a PO becomes a recorded exercise with an audit trail. No new skill, but a loss of informality on what the team currently treats as the quick route.
impacts.process_impact: Added process steps for activity that today has none. The volume is genuinely unknown, so the added effort is unquantified — which is the risk, not the steps themselves.
impacts.tech_impact: New system for activity that currently touches no system at all beyond PO creation.
impacts.other_impacts:
VISIBILITY FINDING: this activity is invisible today. It is absent from event volumes, from cycle-time reporting and from the spend-under-management figure, so any benefit case built on those numbers is built on an incomplete denominator.

This row exists only because a verbatim transcript captured a colleague correcting a headline number in real time (INT-03 @00:02:24). A curated note would have recorded "~150 events per year" and the finding would have been lost.
impacts.benefit_narrative: The quick route stays quick — but it counts, so the team finally gets credit for the volume it actually handles.
impacts.training_timing: T-4 weeks, bundled with TRN-S2C-01 to 04
impacts.key_message: Three-quote jobs go through the system too. It's a lighter path, not the full event process — and it means the work you do finally shows up in the numbers.
impacts.comms_channel: Team workshop with the Procurement Director; job aid
impacts.mitigation_actions: Size this before go-live. Pull 12 months of sub-threshold PO volume from the spend analysis to establish the real number, then confirm with the team whether the design's lighter path actually covers it. If it does not, this becomes an unplanned workload increase on an already-sceptical group in their first weeks on a new system.
impacts.notes: OPEN QUESTION: what is the real annual volume of informal three-quote sourcing? Two Category Managers gave figures 33% apart on the record and neither is recorded anywhere (INT-03 @00:02:24). Nothing in this row can be sized until the spend analysis settles it. Headcount shown is the Category Manager team, not the volume of exercises.

impacts.current_roles: Commercial counsel and legal operations
impacts.as_is: Contracts are Word documents emailed back and forth between the Category Manager and Legal. Version control is by filename convention. There is no structured record of which clauses deviate from standard.
impacts.to_be: Contracts are generated from an approved template against a clause library. Any deviation from a standard clause triggers a mandatory Legal review workflow. Version history and the approval trail are held in the system.
impacts.people_impact: New activity with existing resources: Legal moves from reviewing whole documents on request to reviewing flagged deviations. Volume should fall, but building and maintaining the clause library is new work with no current owner.
impacts.process_impact: Significant change to process steps and to accountability — Legal loses discretion over what reaches them, because the clause library decides.
impacts.tech_impact: New system replacing Word, email and the shared drive for contract authoring.
impacts.other_impacts: Ownership: Legal must own the clause library content, not just review it. Schedule the library build as Legal-led work with programme support, and confirm the ongoing maintenance owner before go-live.
impacts.benefit_narrative: You see the deviations rather than the whole document, and you stop being the version-control mechanism.
impacts.key_message: Contracts are drafted from a clause library and only deviations come to you — which means the library has to say what you would have said.
impacts.comms_channel: Team session; clause library design workshops
impacts.mitigation_actions: Make the clause library build Legal-led, and confirm the maintenance owner before go-live.
impacts.notes: No Legal stakeholder has been interviewed. This row is derived from the process design alone — schedule a Legal session before baselining.

impacts.l4: Named Contract Owner — Expiry Alert Response
impacts.current_roles: Business managers who will be named as Contract Owner — the role does not exist today
impacts.as_is: Contracts sit in shared-drive folders by supplier name with no expiry tracking and no named owner. Lapses are discovered when a supplier calls about a PO that cannot be raised. Nobody has a definitive count of active contracts — around 400 is the working estimate.
impacts.to_be: Every contract is held in the repository with structured metadata and a named Contract Owner. The system issues automated expiry alerts at 180, 90 and 30 days to that owner, who is accountable for renewal or exit.
impacts.people_impact: A new role for ~60 named individuals, with real accountability attached — responding to expiry alerts and owning renewal or exit decisions. It is in nobody's objectives today, and named individuals will start receiving system alerts for a responsibility they have never been told they hold.
impacts.process_impact: Added process steps rather than a redesign: the alert-and-respond cycle is new, but it sits alongside existing work rather than replacing it.
impacts.tech_impact: New system and a new inbox for a population that has never used a contract repository.
impacts.other_impacts: Governance: the accountability needs to land in objectives, not just in the system. An unassigned or unaware owner means the expiry alert goes nowhere and the programme has replaced one silent failure mode with another.
impacts.benefit_narrative: You stop finding out a contract lapsed from the supplier, and renewals become a planned conversation instead of an emergency.
impacts.training_timing: T-3 weeks — cannot precede role assignment
impacts.key_message: You've been named as owner of these contracts. Here's what that means, what the system will send you, and when.
impacts.comms_channel: Personal notification listing the individual's assigned contracts; line-manager briefing; job aid
impacts.mitigation_actions: Assign and confirm Contract Owners with their line managers before go-live, and get the accountability into objectives.
impacts.notes: OPEN QUESTION: the ~60 headcount is extrapolated from ~400 estimated active contracts at roughly 6–7 per owner. Neither the contract count nor the owner population is confirmed — INT-01 records that nobody has a definitive contract count. Contract inventory and owner assignment must both complete before this row can be sized or trained.

impacts.current_roles: Procurement Analyst (single post holder)
impacts.as_is: The Procurement Analyst manually builds a quarterly spend cube and issues it to Category Managers and Finance. This is the role's primary deliverable and the main basis of its standing in the function.
impacts.to_be: Spend analytics is delivered by the platform. Category Managers self-serve dashboards and cost centre owners see live committed spend. The manual quarterly cube is not produced.
impacts.people_impact: The role's primary deliverable is eliminated and FS-02 §3 records that no revised role definition exists. A single post holder whose main output disappears, with nothing yet defined to replace it.
impacts.process_impact: The process is eliminated rather than changed — significant change to steps and to ownership, with the output moving to self-service.
impacts.tech_impact: New system replacing manual extracts and Excel as the analytics toolset.
impacts.other_impacts:
PEOPLE RISK: small population, maximum individual impact — the kind of impact easily missed in a register organised by headcount. This is a line management and HR matter first and a change communication matter second.
OPEN DECISION: define the revised role, or the alternative, before this individual hears about the change through a programme channel.
impacts.benefit_narrative: Cannot be stated credibly until the revised role is defined. Do not attempt a benefit message to this individual before that exists.
impacts.key_message: Handled 1:1 by the line manager, not by programme communication.
impacts.comms_channel: 1:1 with line manager; HR involvement as required
impacts.mitigation_actions: Define the revised role — or the alternative — before this individual hears about the change through a programme channel.
impacts.notes: OPEN QUESTION: what is the revised role definition? FS-02 §3 records that none exists. Needs a Procurement Director decision with HR before any communication to the post holder.

impacts.current_roles: Finance Business Partners supporting UK and PL cost centres
impacts.as_is: Finance issues a monthly commitment report to cost centre owners. Business Partners field questions about it and reconcile discrepancies by hand.
impacts.to_be: Cost centre owners see live committed spend against budget in the system. The monthly commitment report is retired and Business Partners move to advising on the live data rather than producing and explaining a lagging report.
impacts.people_impact: Minimal additional or removed activity, with a small behavioural adjustment: their stakeholders now see the same numbers they do, in real time, which changes the nature of the conversation more than the workload.
impacts.process_impact: Simplified through automation — a manual monthly production task is replaced by live data.
impacts.tech_impact: Gain of system functionality in reporting; the underlying finance toolset is familiar.
impacts.other_impacts: A favourable change for this group — worth carrying in the register so they are informed rather than surprised.
impacts.benefit_narrative: You stop building and defending a monthly report and start advising on numbers your stakeholders can already see.
impacts.key_message: The monthly commitment report is going away — your cost centre owners will see committed spend live, and your role shifts to advising on it.
impacts.comms_channel: Finance team briefing; e-learning

impacts.current_roles: Facilities, IT and Engineering staff handling breakdowns, outages and safety-critical purchases
impacts.as_is: Urgent purchases are handled by phoning a known buyer, who raises the PO immediately and completes the paperwork afterwards. Described in the workshop as 'a phone call and a favour'.
impacts.to_be: Not designed. SIG-01 holds a placeholder task (PH-P2P-015) with no content, and FS-01 §6 records the specification as deferred at design authority on 2026-05-14 with no target date and no owner beyond the workstream lead.
impacts.people_impact: Scored on the assumption that the current informal route closes and is replaced by something more controlled. New activity with existing resources, plus the loss of a trusted personal escalation route.
impacts.process_impact: Significant change to process steps and to accountability — but the to-be does not exist. If nothing is designed, the informal route continues outside the system, undermining the control model and the spend data at the same time.
impacts.tech_impact: New system, with no designed path for the urgent case.
impacts.other_impacts: DESIGN GAP — go-live risk, not a design backlog item. Attendees asked repeatedly how urgent purchases would work and no answer was available (INT-02). Facilities and IT cannot be trained on a process that does not exist, and this is the group most likely to be raising a purchase at 2am on a Sunday. Escalate to the Steering Committee.
impacts.benefit_narrative: Cannot be stated until the process exists.
impacts.training_timing: TBC — cannot be scheduled until the process is designed
impacts.key_message: TBC — this group has asked twice and been given no answer. Silence is itself a message here.
impacts.comms_channel: TBC
impacts.mitigation_actions: Escalate the undesigned emergency path to the Steering Committee as a go-live risk with a required decision date.
impacts.notes: OPEN QUESTION: what is the emergency purchasing process? Deferred at design authority 2026-05-14 (FS-01 §6) with no target date. All scores on this row are provisional and assume a controlled replacement for the current informal route — re-score once the design exists.

impacts.current_roles: Goods-in operatives and warehouse supervisors
impacts.as_is: The warehouse team receipts stock deliveries against the PO using the standard SAP warehouse transaction, working from the printed PO and the delivery note.
impacts.to_be: Unchanged in flow and system — the warehouse transaction and the receipting step stay as they are. What changes is that stock POs now originate in Ariba, so the PO number format and document header look different and the buyer named on the PO may no longer be a person.
impacts.people_impact: No change to the role. Same task, same accountability, same team.
impacts.process_impact: Minor change: the process steps are identical, but the source document looks different and the system of record for the PO changes.
impacts.tech_impact: Same warehouse transaction with a changed document header — no new system for this group.
impacts.other_impacts: Included deliberately: this group is downstream of a major programme and would otherwise hear nothing at all — which is how an unaffected team ends up convinced it has been forgotten.
impacts.benefit_narrative: Nothing changes in how you receipt stock — you'll just see a different PO reference format on the paperwork.
impacts.key_message: Your receipting process isn't changing. PO numbers will look different from January — that's all.
impacts.comms_channel: Team briefing; shift-handover note

impacts.current_roles: Financial accountants running period close
impacts.as_is: Finance builds the goods-received-not-invoiced accrual from an ECC extract, adjusted by hand for the known lag in central goods receipting.
impacts.to_be: Same accrual process and same period-close calendar, sourced from the new system. The manual lag adjustment should reduce as receipting moves to the point of delivery, but the task itself is unchanged.
impacts.people_impact: No change to the role. Same task, same calendar, same accountability.
impacts.process_impact: Minor change to the process: the steps hold, but the data within the process looks different and the system of record changes.
impacts.tech_impact: Same reporting task against a changed source system — fields and extract layout differ.
impacts.other_impacts: Worth carrying because the first period close after go-live is where receipting non-compliance (CI-006) will show up as an accrual variance. Finance should be expecting it rather than investigating it.
impacts.benefit_narrative: The manual lag adjustment shrinks as receipting happens at the point of delivery rather than centrally in arrears.
impacts.key_message: Period close doesn't change. Expect a larger accrual variance in the first two closes while goods receipting beds in.
impacts.comms_channel: Finance team briefing; period-close checklist update
impacts.notes: Derived by inference from the goods receipt redesign rather than from a Finance interview — no period-close stakeholder has been spoken to. Validate with Financial Control.
